item.text:
{
  "schema_version": "formalization-faithfulness-1",
  "role": "blind-translation",
  "dossier_sha256": "62de33638fafec98124c7f90b54e3ad33222e4e8fedc457d80333ae5567b17c5",
  "dependency_coverage": [
    {
      "id": "D001",
      "name": "LocalDef001",
      "meaning": "For a real normed vector space E, a function field : ℝ → E, endpoints left and right, and a vector average, this predicate means left < right and field is interval integrable between these endpoints and average equals LocalDef003 field left right.",
      "effect_on_target": "The conclusion is a conjunction repeating both hypotheses and asserting equality with the specified normalized integral.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D002",
      "name": "LocalDef002",
      "meaning": "The abbreviation sends state, left, and right to LocalDef003 state left right.",
      "effect_on_target": "The candidate average is fixed by definition; the equality in the conclusion reduces to equality of an expression with itself.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D003",
      "name": "LocalDef003",
      "meaning": "The vector obtained by multiplying the oriented interval integral of field from left to right by the real scalar (right − left)⁻¹.",
      "effect_on_target": "Defines the exact candidate average, including its interval orientation and normalization.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D004",
      "name": "Fin",
      "meaning": "Fin m is the finite index type of natural numbers i with 0 ≤ i < m.",
      "effect_on_target": "State values are real coordinate vectors indexed by 0 through m − 1; when m = 0 there are no coordinates.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D005",
      "name": "Fin.fintype",
      "meaning": "Provides a complete finite enumeration of Fin n using List.finRange n.",
      "effect_on_target": "Supplies the finite indexing required by the product norm and normed vector space structures.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D006",
      "name": "InnerProductSpace.toNormedSpace",
      "meaning": "Extracts the underlying normed vector space structure from an inner product space.",
      "effect_on_target": "Supplies the real scalar normed space structure on each real coordinate; no inner product assertion is made.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D007",
      "name": "IntervalIntegrable",
      "meaning": "IntervalIntegrable f μ a b means that f is integrable on (a,b] with respect to μ and also integrable on (b,a] with respect to μ.",
      "effect_on_target": "Both the hypothesis and the conclusion require this conjunction. Since left < right, the second interval is empty.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D008",
      "name": "LT.lt",
      "meaning": "Extracts the strict comparison relation supplied by an LT instance.",
      "effect_on_target": "With Real.instLT, expresses the strict ordering left < right.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D009",
      "name": "MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.volume",
      "meaning": "Extracts the distinguished measure from the selected measure space structure.",
      "effect_on_target": "Fixes the same measure μ from Real.measureSpace for all integrability and integration expressions.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D010",
      "name": "Nat",
      "meaning": "The type of natural numbers, including zero.",
      "effect_on_target": "The proposition quantifies over every finite dimension m, without a positivity assumption.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D011",
      "name": "NonUnitalSeminormedCommRing.toNonUnitalSeminormedRing",
      "meaning": "Extracts a nonunital seminormed ring structure by forgetting the commutativity requirement.",
      "effect_on_target": "Part of the structure conversion supplying the seminormed additive structure on real coordinates; adds no hypothesis.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D012",
      "name": "NonUnitalSeminormedRing.toSeminormedAddCommGroup",
      "meaning": "Retains the norm, additive commutative group, and pseudometric of a nonunital seminormed ring.",
      "effect_on_target": "Provides the additive seminormed structure used to construct the product real normed space.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D013",
      "name": "NormedAddCommGroup.toNormedAddGroup",
      "meaning": "Retains the norm, additive group, and metric while forgetting additive commutativity as a required field.",
      "effect_on_target": "Supplies coordinate normed additive groups for the product structure used in the integrability hypothesis.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D014",
      "name": "NormedAddGroup.toENormedAddMonoid",
      "meaning": "Builds an extended-normed additive monoid from a normed additive group using its associated continuous extended norm and addition.",
      "effect_on_target": "Provides the extended norm structure required by IntervalIntegrable on the vector-valued state.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D015",
      "name": "NormedCommRing.toSeminormedCommRing",
      "meaning": "Retains the norm, ring operations, and pseudometric of a normed commutative ring as a seminormed commutative ring.",
      "effect_on_target": "Participates in constructing the real coordinate seminormed additive structure without changing its operations.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D016",
      "name": "Pi.normedAddCommGroup",
      "meaning": "Constructs the normed additive commutative group of a finite family of coordinate groups, using the norm and pseudometric inherited from Pi.seminormedAddGroup.",
      "effect_on_target": "Makes Fin m → ℝ the normed additive commutative group in which the average and integral take values.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D017",
      "name": "Pi.normedAddGroup",
      "meaning": "Constructs a normed additive group on a finite product, retaining the norm, addition, and pseudometric from Pi.seminormedAddGroup.",
      "effect_on_target": "Provides the product normed group underlying the integrability hypothesis.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D018",
      "name": "Pi.normedSpace",
      "meaning": "Constructs a normed vector space on a finite product using the product module structure.",
      "effect_on_target": "Supplies coordinatewise real scalar multiplication on Fin m → ℝ, including multiplication by (right − left)⁻¹.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D019",
      "name": "Pi.topologicalSpace",
      "meaning": "Defines the product topology through the topologies induced by all coordinate evaluation maps.",
      "effect_on_target": "Uses the product of the real coordinate topologies for the state integrability condition.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D020",
      "name": "PseudoMetricSpace.toUniformSpace",
      "meaning": "Extracts the uniform space underlying a pseudometric space.",
      "effect_on_target": "Transfers the real metric structure into the topology used on each coordinate.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D021",
      "name": "RCLike.toInnerProductSpaceReal",
      "meaning": "Builds a real inner product space on an RCLike field using its real inner product and underlying normed algebra.",
      "effect_on_target": "For ℝ, supplies an intermediate structure used to obtain the normed space of real coordinates; the target asserts no inner product property.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D022",
      "name": "Real",
      "meaning": "The type of real numbers.",
      "effect_on_target": "The independent variable, endpoints, scalar coefficients, and every state coordinate are real.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D023",
      "name": "Real.instLT",
      "meaning": "Supplies the strict order relation on ℝ through Real.lt.",
      "effect_on_target": "Requires the left endpoint to be strictly smaller than the right endpoint.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D024",
      "name": "Real.instRCLike",
      "meaning": "Equips ℝ with an RCLike structure whose real-part map is the identity, imaginary-part map is zero, and distinguished imaginary element is zero.",
      "effect_on_target": "Supports the real coordinate normed space construction; introduces no complex coordinates or extra variables.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D025",
      "name": "Real.measureSpace",
      "meaning": "A fixed measure space instance on ℝ, supplied here only by inferInstance; the resolved measure construction is not displayed.",
      "effect_on_target": "Determines μ for both integrability and the average. Its identification and normalization as a particular concrete measure cannot be checked from the displayed body.",
      "status": "unclear"
    },
    {
      "id": "D026",
      "name": "Real.normedAddCommGroup",
      "meaning": "Equips ℝ with its real norm, additive commutative group, and metric.",
      "effect_on_target": "Supplies the normed additive structure on every coordinate and the underlying norm used by the product construction.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D027",
      "name": "Real.normedCommRing",
      "meaning": "Combines the real normed additive commutative group with the real commutative ring operations and their norm compatibility.",
      "effect_on_target": "Provides the structural source for the real seminormed additive groups used in Pi.normedSpace.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D028",
      "name": "Real.normedField",
      "meaning": "Equips ℝ with field operations and its norm, including multiplicative norm compatibility and the total inverse convention inv_zero.",
      "effect_on_target": "Makes ℝ the scalar normed field. The strict endpoint inequality ensures that the particular scalar being inverted is nonzero.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D029",
      "name": "Real.pseudoMetricSpace",
      "meaning": "Defines real distance by d(x,y) = |x − y|, with the associated uniform structure.",
      "effect_on_target": "Fixes the usual metric topology on the real coordinates used by the product topology.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D030",
      "name": "SeminormedCommRing.toNonUnitalSeminormedCommRing",
      "meaning": "Retains the seminorm, additive operations, multiplication, and pseudometric while forgetting the requirement of a multiplicative identity.",
      "effect_on_target": "An intermediate conversion in the real coordinate structure; adds no restriction to state.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D031",
      "name": "UniformSpace.toTopologicalSpace",
      "meaning": "Extracts the topology associated with a uniform space.",
      "effect_on_target": "Completes the passage from the real metric to the coordinate topology in the integrability hypothesis.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D032",
      "name": "And",
      "meaning": "Logical conjunction: both propositions must hold.",
      "effect_on_target": "Combines the strict endpoint inequality, interval integrability, and average equality; also combines the two integrability conditions in IntervalIntegrable.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D033",
      "name": "Eq",
      "meaning": "Equality of two objects of the same type.",
      "effect_on_target": "Requires exact equality of coordinate vectors, equivalently equality at every index, between the candidate average and its defining expression.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D034",
      "name": "NormedAddCommGroup",
      "meaning": "A commutative additive group equipped with a norm and compatible metric.",
      "effect_on_target": "Provides the additive and analytic structure needed for vector integration and LocalDef001; the target uses the specified finite product instance.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D035",
      "name": "NormedAddCommGroup.toSeminormedAddCommGroup",
      "meaning": "Retains a normed additive commutative group's norm, additive operations, and pseudometric as a seminormed structure.",
      "effect_on_target": "Makes the same vector norm and addition available to the generic normed space and topology constructions.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D036",
      "name": "NormedSpace",
      "meaning": "A vector space over a normed field whose scalar action satisfies the required norm compatibility.",
      "effect_on_target": "Allows real scalar multiplication of the vector-valued integral and supplies the module used in LocalDef003.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D037",
      "name": "SeminormedAddCommGroup.toPseudoMetricSpace",
      "meaning": "Extracts the pseudometric structure of a seminormed additive commutative group.",
      "effect_on_target": "Provides the norm-derived analytic topology needed by the generic definitions.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D038",
      "name": "AddMonoid.toAddZeroClass",
      "meaning": "Retains addition, zero, and the left and right additive identity laws of an additive monoid.",
      "effect_on_target": "Supplies underlying zero and addition infrastructure for vector scalar multiplication and integration.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D039",
      "name": "AddZero.toZero",
      "meaning": "Extracts the distinguished zero element from an additive structure with zero.",
      "effect_on_target": "Provides the zero vector used by the underlying algebraic and integral structures.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D040",
      "name": "AddZeroClass.toAddZero",
      "meaning": "Extracts addition and zero while forgetting the additive identity laws as explicit fields.",
      "effect_on_target": "An intermediate projection supplying the zero vector; imposes no additional proposition.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D041",
      "name": "DistribMulAction.toDistribSMul",
      "meaning": "Retains scalar multiplication and its preservation of zero and addition from a distributive multiplicative action.",
      "effect_on_target": "Passes the real vector space scalar action toward the scalar multiplication operation used to normalize the integral.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D042",
      "name": "DistribSMul.toSMulZeroClass",
      "meaning": "Extracts scalar multiplication together with preservation of zero.",
      "effect_on_target": "Part of the projection chain exposing the existing real scalar action.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D043",
      "name": "ENormedAddCommMonoid.toESeminormedAddCommMonoid",
      "meaning": "Extracts the extended-seminormed additive commutative monoid underlying an extended-normed one.",
      "effect_on_target": "Provides weaker analytic and additive infrastructure for the same vector space without changing its operations.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D044",
      "name": "ESeminormedAddCommMonoid.toAddCommMonoid",
      "meaning": "Retains the additive commutative monoid of an extended-seminormed additive commutative monoid.",
      "effect_on_target": "Supplies commutative vector addition and zero for the module-related structures.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D045",
      "name": "ESeminormedAddCommMonoid.toESeminormedAddMonoid",
      "meaning": "Extracts the extended-seminormed additive monoid while forgetting the commutativity requirement.",
      "effect_on_target": "Part of the structure chain supplying the vector additive monoid.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D046",
      "name": "ESeminormedAddMonoid.toAddMonoid",
      "meaning": "Extracts the additive monoid underlying an extended-seminormed additive monoid.",
      "effect_on_target": "Makes the same vector addition and zero available to scalar action constructions.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D047",
      "name": "HSMul.hSMul",
      "meaning": "Extracts the scalar multiplication operation from a heterogeneous scalar multiplication instance.",
      "effect_on_target": "Applies the real reciprocal of the interval length to the vector-valued integral.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D048",
      "name": "HSub.hSub",
      "meaning": "Extracts the subtraction operation from a heterogeneous subtraction instance.",
      "effect_on_target": "Expresses right − left in the normalization and the difference of the two restricted integrals in intervalIntegral.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D049",
      "name": "Inv.inv",
      "meaning": "Extracts the inverse operation from an inverse instance.",
      "effect_on_target": "Forms the real reciprocal (right − left)⁻¹.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D050",
      "name": "Module.toDistribMulAction",
      "meaning": "Extracts the distributive multiplicative scalar action underlying a module.",
      "effect_on_target": "Ensures the scalar multiplication in the average is the one from the selected real vector space.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D051",
      "name": "NormedAddCommGroup.toENormedAddCommMonoid",
      "meaning": "Builds an extended-normed additive commutative monoid from a normed additive commutative group, preserving its additive structure and using its associated extended norm.",
      "effect_on_target": "Supplies the analytic and additive structures needed inside the generic definitions.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D052",
      "name": "NormedSpace.toModule",
      "meaning": "Extracts the module underlying a normed vector space.",
      "effect_on_target": "Provides the real scalar multiplication used in LocalDef003.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D053",
      "name": "Real.instInv",
      "meaning": "Supplies the real inverse operation through Real.inv'.",
      "effect_on_target": "Specifies that the normalization uses inversion in ℝ; under left < right this is the reciprocal of a positive length.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D054",
      "name": "Real.instMonoid",
      "meaning": "Supplies the multiplicative monoid structure on ℝ by instance inference.",
      "effect_on_target": "Supports composition and identity of real scalar actions; no separate monoid variable or hypothesis is introduced.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D055",
      "name": "Real.instSub",
      "meaning": "Defines real subtraction a − b as a + (−b).",
      "effect_on_target": "Fixes the denominator as right plus the negation of left.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D056",
      "name": "Real.semiring",
      "meaning": "Supplies the semiring structure on ℝ by instance inference.",
      "effect_on_target": "Provides scalar arithmetic required by the real module structure.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D057",
      "name": "SMulZeroClass.toSMul",
      "meaning": "Extracts scalar multiplication from a scalar action that preserves zero.",
      "effect_on_target": "Exposes the scalar multiplication subsequently used by instHSMul.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D058",
      "name": "instHSMul",
      "meaning": "Uses an ordinary scalar multiplication operation as a heterogeneous scalar multiplication with unchanged target type.",
      "effect_on_target": "The normalization produces another vector in Fin m → ℝ.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D059",
      "name": "instHSub",
      "meaning": "Uses ordinary subtraction as heterogeneous subtraction with all three types equal.",
      "effect_on_target": "Preserves the usual subtraction operations on reals and on the vector space.",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "id": "D060",
      "name": "intervalIntegral",
      "meaning": "The oriented interval integral of f from a to b with respect to μ is the integral of f against μ restricted to (a,b], minus its integral against μ restricted to (b,a].",
      "effect_on_target": "Since left < right, the reverse interval is empty, so the average is the integral over (left,right] scaled by the reciprocal of right − left.",
      "status": "understood"
    }
  ],
  "translation": {
    "binders": [
      "For every natural number m, including m = 0.",
      "For every function state : ℝ → (Fin m → ℝ), assigning a real coordinate vector to each real argument.",
      "For every pair of real endpoints left and right.",
      "The explicit proof binders hcell and hstate witness the two hypotheses; they introduce no additional mathematical objects or existential choices."
    ],
    "hypotheses": [
      "left < right.",
      "State is interval integrable with respect to μ, where μ is the measure selected by Real.measureSpace.volume: state is integrable on (left,right] and on (right,left]."
    ],
    "conclusions": [
      "left < right.",
      "State is integrable with respect to μ on both (left,right] and (right,left].",
      "The prescribed vector LocalDef002 state left right equals (right − left)⁻¹ times the oriented interval integral of state from left to right with respect to μ. By the definition of LocalDef002, both sides are the same expression."
    ],
    "mathematical_definitions": [
      "Write V = Fin m → ℝ, the real vector space of m coordinates, with the supplied finite product normed group structure, product topology, and coordinatewise vector operations.",
      "Write μ for the distinguished measure extracted from Real.measureSpace.",
      "For a function f : ℝ → V, define J(f,a,b) = ∫ f d(μ restricted to (a,b]) − ∫ f d(μ restricted to (b,a]).",
      "Define A(f,a,b) = (b − a)⁻¹ · J(f,a,b), where the dot denotes real scalar multiplication of a vector.",
      "LocalDef003 f a b is A(f,a,b), and LocalDef002 state left right is exactly A(state,left,right).",
      "LocalDef001 f a b v means (a < b) ∧ (IntervalIntegrable f μ a b ∧ v = A(f,a,b)).",
      "Under left < right, (right,left] is empty and A(state,left,right) = (right − left)⁻¹ · ∫ state d(μ restricted to (left,right])."
    ],
    "proposition_plain_english": "For every finite dimension m, every real-vector-valued function state on ℝ, and every pair of real numbers left < right such that state is interval integrable with respect to the fixed measure μ, the vector defined to be (right − left)⁻¹ times the oriented interval integral of state satisfies the predicate requiring these same endpoint and integrability conditions and equality to that same normalized integral. Expanded completely, the assertion is that the two given hypotheses imply their conjunction with A(state,left,right) = A(state,left,right)."
  },
  "restrictions_and_vacuity_risks": [
    "Only strictly ordered endpoints are covered. Equal or reversed endpoints cannot satisfy the antecedent; the asserted averaging interpretation therefore never uses a zero or negative interval length.",
    "No positive-dimension assumption appears. For m = 0, the vector space contains just the empty coordinate function, and coordinatewise equalities have no coordinates to check.",
    "The integrability assumption concerns the stated intervals only. No global integrability, continuity, differentiability, boundedness, or differential equation is assumed.",
    "The reverse interval (right,left] is empty under the endpoint hypothesis, so its integrability requirement is automatic.",
    "The conclusion repeats the assumptions and adds a definitional identity. It establishes no independent property beyond this packaging.",
    "There is no existential witness, selected sample point, claim that the average is attained by state, positivity claim, error estimate, approximation bound, or dynamical interpretation.",
    "The function is defined on all of ℝ, but the displayed integral expressions depend only on its values on the two specified intervals, through measure-theoretic integration.",
    "The normalization is by the real endpoint difference right − left, not explicitly by μ((left,right]). Equating those two quantities requires information about the selected measure."
  ],
  "ambiguities": [
    "D025 displays only inferInstance, so the packet does not expose the resolved construction or normalization of Real.measureSpace. The exact translation therefore keeps its selected measure as μ rather than independently certifying that it is Lebesgue measure.",
    "Some external semantic boundaries remain unexpanded, including MeasureTheory.IntegrableOn, MeasureTheory.integral, and Pi.seminormedAddGroup. The translation uses their conventional integrability, integral, and finite product structure roles; their internal definitions, totalization conventions, and exact product norm formula cannot be independently checked from the packet."
  ]
}
